    A good pair in every window of 3 dim k(P) arrows #

    Let d be the number of nonzero morphisms of P, the dimension of k(P). Every point of a window pt 0, …, pt N of a line has a nonzero morphism to a sink of the window (WLine.WSink), unless it lies on the initial backward run (cover_or_run). Points with the same sink are told apart by the value of this morphism, and the points of the initial run by the value of their morphism to pt 0. If no good pair lies in the window, at most two sinks of the window have the same image in P (goodPair_of_three), so N + 1 ≤ 2d + d. Hence a window of 3d arrows contains a good pair (exists_goodPair_window; BO13b, Lemma 7.2 (b), with the count of BO23, proof of Theorem 7).

    def LargeIndecomposable.RayCat.WLine.WSink {P : Type} [CategoryTheory.Category.{0, 0} P] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms P] [IsRayCategory P] {x₀ : P} (L : WLine x₀) (N s : ℕ) :
    Prop

    A sink of the window pt 0, …, pt N at the point pt s: the arrow on its left points to it, and so does the arrow on its right unless s = N.
